newsitem.title: USA: Movie set construction uncovers Civil War site.
newsitem.headline: Movie set construction uncovers Civil War site.

text.p: Contractors building a movie studio in Virginia found an underground tunnel that historians said Thursday was a mine used by Confederate troops during the Civil War.

Chris Calkins, a historian at the Petersburg National Battlefield, which is south of the mine site, said a section of the mine would have been filled with kegs of gunpowder to be ignited in case of an attack by the Union Army.

The mine's existence was corroborated by research on the Civil War. It described a tunnel stretching from the Confederate trenches to a nearby house, which during the Civil War was owned by a Doctor Duval, Calkins said.
"The company that's building Millenium Studios did ground-penetrating radar and has determined the scope of the tunnel and it heads right to the house," he said.
The mine was filled with water when it was found.

Petersburg National Battlefield, the site of a 292-day siege, is best known for the Battle of the Crater, a stunning Union Army defeat on July 30, 1864, in which northern troops tried to blast their way through Confederate lines by detonating explosives placed at the end of the mine.
Calkins said the construction company would avoid the mine.
"We'll probably continue to study it," he said. "... Fortunately, it is not located anywhere where they are doing any construction."
The Civil War was fought between Americans from 1861 to 1865. It began when seven pro-slavery southern states seceded from the nation and formed the Confederate States of America.
The war ended with a Union victory over the Confederacy, when 27,000 Confederate troops surrendered in Appomattox, Va.
